questions.title: Product Code Digit Analysis
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Extract digits arithmetically to compute a count, a sum, and a maximum in one loop.
questions.problem_statement: A warehouse needs to analyze a positive numeric product code. Given an integer N, print its digit count, digit sum, and largest digit on separate lines. Do not convert the number to a string.
questions.output_format: Three lines containing the digit count, digit sum, and largest digit.
hints: n % 10 gives the last digit and n / 10 removes it.
Update three variables in the same loop: count, sum, and max.
Because N is at least 1, the loop runs at least once.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Three lines containing the digit count, digit sum, and largest digit.

questions.title: Alternating Digit Balance
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Alternate between two running sums while extracting digits from the right.
questions.problem_statement: A numeric code is balanced when the sum of digits at odd positions from the right equals the sum of digits at even positions from the right. Positions begin at 1. Read N as an integer and determine whether it is balanced.
questions.input_format: One positive integer N, where 1 ≤ N ≤ 10⁹.
questions.output_format: Print Balanced or Not Balanced.
hints: Keep a position counter that starts at 1 and increases with every digit.
Add the digit to oddSum when the position is odd and to evenSum when it is even.
Compare the two sums after the loop.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.input_format: One positive integer N, where 1 ≤ N ≤ 10⁹.
extra_fields.output_format: Print Balanced or Not Balanced.

questions.title: Numeric Palindrome Validator
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Reverse a number arithmetically and compare it with the original.
questions.problem_statement: A numeric identifier is a palindrome if it reads the same forward and backward. Determine whether a non-negative integer is a palindrome using arithmetic operations, without converting it to a string. Leading zeros are not part of an integer's representation.
questions.output_format: Print Palindrome or Not Palindrome.
hints: Keep a copy of N, because the loop will reduce the working value to 0.
Build the reverse with reversed = reversed * 10 + digit.
Store the reverse in a long: reversing 1000000000 is safe, but other 10-digit values can exceed int.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print Palindrome or Not Palindrome.

questions.title: Prime Number Validator
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Test primality efficiently by checking divisors only up to the square root.
questions.problem_statement: An identifier is prime if it is greater than 1 and has exactly two positive divisors. Given N, determine whether it is prime. Use divisor checks and handle values below 2 correctly.
questions.output_format: Print Prime or Not Prime.
hints: Return Not Prime immediately for N < 2.
A composite number always has a divisor d with d * d <= N.
Stop at the first divisor you find.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print Prime or Not Prime.

questions.title: Power-of-Two Batch Size
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Use repeated division to test whether a number is a power of two.
questions.problem_statement: A storage system only accepts batch sizes that are powers of two: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and so on. Determine whether N is a power of two by repeatedly dividing it by 2. Do not use logarithms or built-in methods.
questions.output_format: Print Power of Two or Not Power of Two.
hints: Read N as a long.
While N is even, divide it by 2.
N is a power of two exactly when the loop ends with N equal to 1.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print Power of Two or Not Power of Two.

questions.title: Greatest Common Divisor and Least Common Multiple
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Compute a GCD with the Euclidean algorithm and derive the LCM without overflow.
questions.problem_statement: Given two positive integers A and B, calculate their greatest common divisor (GCD) and least common multiple (LCM). Use the Euclidean algorithm for GCD. Calculate the LCM using (A / GCD) * B and store it in a long, because the result may exceed the int range.
questions.input_format: Two positive integers A and B, each on a separate line, where 1 ≤ A, B ≤ 10⁹.
questions.output_format: Print the GCD on the first line and the LCM on the second line.
hints: Keep the original A and B; the Euclidean loop changes its working copies.
Loop while b != 0: remainder = a % b; a = b; b = remainder;.
Divide before multiplying: (A / gcd) * B, computed in long.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.input_format: Two positive integers A and B, each on a separate line, where 1 ≤ A, B ≤ 10⁹.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the GCD on the first line and the LCM on the second line.

questions.title: Perfect-Square Detector
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Search for an integer square root with a loop instead of Math.sqrt().
questions.problem_statement: A non-negative integer is a perfect square if it equals k × k for some non-negative integer k. Determine whether N is a perfect square without using Math.sqrt() or floating-point calculations.
questions.output_format: Print Perfect Square or Not Perfect Square.
hints: Try k = 0, 1, 2, ... while k * k <= N.
If k * k == N for some k, N is a perfect square.
Use long for k * k so the comparison never overflows.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print Perfect Square or Not Perfect Square.

questions.title: Armstrong Number Validator
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Count digits first, then raise each digit to that power in a second pass.
questions.problem_statement: A positive integer is an Armstrong number if the sum of its digits, each raised to the total number of digits, equals the original number. Determine whether N satisfies this property.
questions.output_format: Print Armstrong or Not Armstrong.
hints: Count the digits in a first loop using a copy of N.
In a second loop, raise each digit to that power with a small inner loop rather than Math.pow().
Every single-digit number is an Armstrong number, because d to the power 1 is d.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print Armstrong or Not Armstrong.

questions.title: Prime Neighbours Within a Range
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Search a range in both directions for the nearest primes, handling the empty case.
questions.problem_statement: Given A and B, find the smallest prime strictly greater than A and the largest prime strictly less than B. Both primes must lie strictly inside the interval (A, B). If no prime exists in the interval, print Not Found for both results.
questions.input_format: A and B on separate lines, where 0 ≤ A < B ≤ 10⁶.
questions.output_format: Print the smallest qualifying prime on the first line and the largest on the second line. If none exists, print Not Found on both lines.
hints: Search upward from A + 1 and stop at the first prime below B.
Search downward from B - 1 and stop at the first prime above A.
If the upward search finds nothing, the downward search will not either, so both lines are Not Found.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.input_format: A and B on separate lines, where 0 ≤ A < B ≤ 10⁶.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the smallest qualifying prime on the first line and the largest on the second line. If none exists, print Not Found on both lines.

questions.title: Strong Number Detector
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Combine digit extraction with a factorial helper method.
questions.problem_statement: A positive integer is strong if the sum of the factorials of its digits equals the number itself. Define 0! as 1. Determine whether N is a strong number.
questions.output_format: Print Strong or Not Strong.
hints: Write a helper method static int factorial(int d) for a single digit.
Add factorial(digit) for each digit, using a copy of N in the loop.
The factorial loop returns 1 when d is 0, which matches 0! = 1.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print Strong or Not Strong.

questions.title: Digital Root Calculator
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Nest a digit-sum loop inside a loop that repeats until one digit remains.
questions.problem_statement: Repeatedly add the digits of a positive integer until the result is a single digit. Print that final digit. Use arithmetic operations rather than string conversion.
questions.output_format: Print the digital root.
hints: Read N as a long.
The outer loop runs while n > 9.
The inner loop replaces n with the sum of its digits.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the digital root.

questions.title: Fibonacci Threshold Monitor
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Generate a sequence with two rolling variables and track the position of each term.
questions.problem_statement:
The Fibonacci sequence begins with 0 and 1, and each subsequent term is the sum of the previous two terms. Find the first term greater than or equal to a target T. Print the term and its zero-based position, with the initial 0 at position 0.

Use long for the sequence values. For every allowed T, the answer is reached before the sequence exceeds the long range.
questions.output_format: Print the first qualifying Fibonacci term and its position, separated by a space.
hints: Keep the current term, the next term, and the position in three variables.
Loop while current < T; in each step, shift the pair forward and increase the position.
T = 0 is answered immediately by the term 0 at position 0.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the first qualifying Fibonacci term and its position, separated by a space.

questions.title: Prime Factorization of a Number
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Divide out each factor repeatedly and stop trial division at the square root.
questions.problem_statement: Express a positive integer as a product of prime factors. Print all prime factors in non-decreasing order, repeating a factor as many times as it occurs. Do not use arrays or built-in prime-factorization libraries.
questions.output_format: Print the prime factors separated by single spaces.
hints: Try divisors d starting at 2, and divide N by d for as long as it divides evenly.
Only test while d * d <= N; whatever remains above 1 afterwards is itself a prime factor.
Build the output with a space before every factor except the first.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the prime factors separated by single spaces.

questions.title: Collatz Sequence Step Counter
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Loop until a condition is met when the number of iterations is not known in advance.
questions.problem_statement: Start with a positive integer N. If it is even, divide it by 2. If it is odd, replace it with 3 × N + 1. Repeat until the value becomes 1. Count the number of transformations, not the number of terms. Use long for intermediate values.
questions.output_format: Print the number of transformations required to reach 1.
hints: Use a while loop that runs until the value equals 1.
Store the value in a long; some starting values below 10⁶ climb past the int range.
For N = 1, no transformation is needed, so the answer is 0.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the number of transformations required to reach 1.

questions.title: Count Numbers With Exactly Three Divisors
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Use a number-theory property to replace a slow brute-force search.
questions.problem_statement: Count the integers in the inclusive range [L, R] that have exactly three positive divisors. A number has exactly three positive divisors if and only if it is the square of a prime number. Use this property to avoid checking every possible divisor of every number.
questions.input_format: L and R on separate lines, where 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 10⁹.
questions.output_format: Print the count of numbers with exactly three positive divisors.
hints: Loop over candidate primes p instead of over the numbers in the range.
Continue while p * p <= R, using long for p * p.
Count p when it is prime and p * p >= L.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.input_format: L and R on separate lines, where 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 10⁹.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the count of numbers with exactly three positive divisors.

questions.title: Decimal to Octal Converter
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Convert to another base with repeated division, building the digits in the right order.
questions.problem_statement: Convert a non-negative decimal integer to its octal (base-8) representation using repeated division and remainders. Do not use built-in base-conversion methods. You may use a String to store and reverse the generated digits. The output must not contain leading zeros, except that input 0 produces output 0.
questions.output_format: Print the octal representation.
hints: n % 8 gives the next octal digit from the right, and n / 8 removes it.
Prepend each digit to a String: result = digit + result;.
Handle N = 0 separately, because the loop does not run for it.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the octal representation.

questions.title: Abundant, Perfect, or Deficient
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Sum proper divisors efficiently in divisor pairs and classify the result.
questions.problem_statement:
For a positive integer N, calculate the sum of its proper divisors (positive divisors smaller than N). Classify the number as:
- Abundant if the sum is greater than N.
- Perfect if the sum equals N.
- Deficient if the sum is less than N.
questions.output_format: Print the corresponding classification.
hints: Divisors come in pairs: if d divides N, so does N / d.
Loop d from 2 while d * d <= N, adding both d and N / d, but add a square root only once.
Start the sum at 1 for N > 1, and remember that 1 has no proper divisors, so its sum is 0.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the corresponding classification.

questions.title: Consecutive Prime Sum Counter
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Combine nested loops and a prime helper to enumerate runs of consecutive primes.
questions.problem_statement:
A mathematical analysis tool investigates whether N can be represented as the sum of two or more consecutive prime numbers. Count all distinct representations. The primes must appear in increasing order, and no prime may be skipped within a representation.

For example, 2 + 3 + 5 is valid, but 2 + 5 is not because 3 is skipped.
questions.output_format: Print the number of valid representations.
hints: Write an isPrime helper and a nextPrime helper that returns the first prime greater than its argument.
For each starting prime p, keep adding the following primes until the sum reaches or passes N.
Count a run only if the sum equals N exactly and the run has at least two primes.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print the number of valid representations.

questions.title: Amicable Number Pair Search
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Reuse a divisor-sum method to find and print each amicable pair exactly once.
questions.problem_statement:
Two distinct positive integers A and B form an amicable pair if the sum of the proper divisors of A equals B and the sum of the proper divisors of B equals A.

Given an upper limit N, find all amicable pairs for which both numbers are at most N. Print each pair once, with the smaller number first, ordered by increasing smaller number. Do not use arrays or collections.
questions.output_format: Print each pair as A B on a separate line. If no pair exists, print No Pairs.
hints: Write a method that returns the sum of the proper divisors of a number.
For each a, let b = properDivisorSum(a); a pair exists when b > a, b <= N, and properDivisorSum(b) == a.
Requiring b > a prints each pair once and skips perfect numbers, where b equals a.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.output_format: Print each pair as A B on a separate line. If no pair exists, print No Pairs.

questions.title: Range-Wide Digit Property Analyzer
questions.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
questions.objective: Combine digit-sum and prime-test helpers to filter every number in a range.
questions.problem_statement:
A positive integer qualifies when both conditions hold:
1. Its digit sum is a prime number.
2. The integer is divisible by its digit sum.
Count all qualifying integers in the inclusive range [L, R]. Do not convert the numbers to strings or use arrays.
questions.input_format: L and R on separate lines, where 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 10⁵.
questions.output_format: Print the number of qualifying integers.
hints: Write two helpers: digitSum(int n) and isPrime(int n).
For each number, compute the digit sum once and store it in a variable.
Check primality of the digit sum, then check number % digitSum == 0.

extra_fields.module: Module 07: Number Problems with Loops and Methods
extra_fields.input_format: L and R on separate lines, where 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 10⁵.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the number of qualifying integers.
